Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Aegis CyberSecure Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question queue will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aegis CyberSecure's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Aegis CyberSecure had a strong third quarter, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our Aegis Sentinel platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: accelerating our AI-driven XDR platform adoption, expanding our Zero Trust orchestration in multi-cloud environments, fortifying ransomware resilience through our Endpoint Fortress suite, and scaling our global footprint with a focus on high-growth regions. These initiatives are delivering measurable value, driving 28% year-over-year revenue growth in our strategic product lines and expanding our annual recurring revenue to $1.2 billion, up 35% from last year.

First, on our AI-driven Extended Detection and Response platform, Aegis Sentinel. We've experienced explosive traction, fueled by the industry's shift toward unified threat intelligence amid a 62% surge in sophisticated advanced persistent threat attacks, according to Mandiant's M-Trends 2024 report. In Q3 alone, we onboarded 450 new enterprise customers, including Fortune 500 names like a major U.S. financial institution and a European automotive original equipment manufacturer, bringing our Sentinel deployment base to over 4,200 organizations. Key metrics include an average mean time to detect of 17 minutes for our customers—down 40% quarter-over-quarter—powered by our proprietary NeuroThreat AI engine, which now processes 2.5 petabytes of telemetry daily across endpoints, networks, and cloud workloads. We've integrated generative AI for automated playbook generation, cutting analyst fatigue by 55% in beta trials. This positions us ahead of competitors like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks' Cortex XDR, with our platform's false positive rate under 0.3%, compared to the industry average of 1.2%. Moving forward, we're targeting 50% XDR revenue growth in fiscal 2025 as we launch Sentinel QuantumShield, our post-quantum cryptography module to address harvest-now-decrypt-later threats.

Next, our Zero Trust Architecture orchestration, especially via Aegis Nexus, our SASE-plus platform. Adoption has picked up speed as enterprises navigate hybrid workforces and expanding multi-cloud setups—Gartner forecasts 75% of organizations adopting Zero Trust by 2026. We've posted a 42% quarter-over-quarter increase in Nexus subscriptions, with annual recurring revenue from this segment reaching $320 million, or 27% of total recurring revenue. A highlight was our deepened partnership with AWS, where Nexus now integrates natively with Amazon GuardDuty and Bedrock for seamless identity-centric access controls, securing more than 1.2 million workloads in Q3. North America accounts for 62% of Nexus deployments, but EMEA grew 68% year-over-year, propelled by GDPR compliance needs and wins with two DAX 40 banks. In APAC, we're up 55%, balancing slower Japan momentum with rapid gains in India and Southeast Asia through hyperscaler alliances like Alibaba Cloud. Beyond connectivity, Nexus delivers 3.7 times return on security investments via micro-segmentation that stops 98% of lateral movement, as validated by an independent Forrester Total Economic Impact study. We're committing an additional $150 million in R&D, announced today, to Nexus Edge, bolstering operational technology and Internet of Things Zero Trust for manufacturing sectors vulnerable to Log4Shell-style flaws.

On ransomware resilience through Endpoint Fortress, our enhanced endpoint detection and response solution featuring behavioral analytics and automated decryption capabilities. With Chainalysis noting $1.1 billion in ransomware payouts already this year, this remains critical. In Q3, Fortress licenses surged 320% year-over-year, now safeguarding 850,000 endpoints worldwide, and we blocked 14,500 ransomware attempts—a 112% jump from Q2—with a 99.7% prevention rate. Our DecryptAI feature restored $45 million in customer data value without ransom payments, giving us a lead over peers like SentinelOne. Customer Net Promoter Scores reached 78, highlighted by healthcare successes under HIPAA scrutiny. U.S. public sector deals rose 75%, echoing Colonial Pipeline concerns, while Latin America expanded 90% against Conti and LockBit strains. We're now incorporating supply chain risk management, scanning over 500,000 third-party components daily to learn from SolarWinds and MOVEit incidents. This contributed to a 15% gross margin expansion to 82%.

Lastly, global scaling and mergers and acquisitions. We've reached 22 countries, with APAC revenue at 18% of total—up from 12% last year—via our Singapore hub and Tencent Cloud partnerships. EMEA contributes 25%, strengthened by acquiring UK-based ThreatLynx for $180 million, which adds behavioral biometrics to our identity portfolio and boosts our EU engineering team by 120. Our M&A pipeline stands at $500 million, eyeing operational technology security in the $15 billion industrial control systems market per IDC. Headcount grew 22% to 3,800, with 40% in R&D, and retention at 95% despite talent competition.

Overall, these efforts yielded 150 basis points of market share growth to 4.8% in the $60 billion cybersecurity market, according to IDC. We're shaping the future, with Q4 outlook at 25-30% growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we delivered a strong third quarter. Revenue reached $1.25 billion, up 28% year-over-year. This momentum spanned all product lines. Gross margins expanded to 82%, while operating expenses totaled $850 million. Net income was $280 million, or $1.45 per diluted share.

Turning to customer metrics, our Net Dollar Retention rate—or NDR—stood at 122% for Q3, up 500 basis points from 117% in the prior year and our 11th consecutive quarter above 120%. This surpasses the industry average of 110-115%, as noted in Bessemer Venture Partners' recent reports, aligning us with top performers like CrowdStrike at 118% and Zscaler at 115%. NDR captures revenue retention and expansion from the prior year's customer cohort over 12 months, starting from about $450 million in beginning ARR.

Expansions accounted for +28%, with over 65% of our top 1,000 customers—driving 80% of recurring revenue—growing their deployments. Our AI-powered Aegis Sentinel XDR saw 42% attachment among endpoint users upgrading from legacy sensors. A Fortune 100 financial firm, for instance, added Cloud Workload Protection for AWS and Azure hybrids, lifting spend 35% year-over-year. Zero Trust Network Access ties with Okta and Microsoft Entra ID spurred cross-sells as firms ditch VPNs amid SASE growth—Gartner sees SASE at $11 billion by 2025.

Contractions and churn dragged just -2%, with gross retention excluding churn at 124% and churn below 1.5% versus industry 5-7%. High switching costs from our 99.999% uptime agents and MITRE ATT&CK mapping deter changes, especially post-incidents like Change Healthcare, where our playbooks secured expansions.

Regionally: North America at 60% of ARR delivered 125% NDR, driven by CISA zero-trust rules and healthcare/infrastructure defenses against LockBit and BlackCat. EMEA hit 120%, boosted by NIS2 and GDPR options in Frankfurt/London data centers—a European telco grew 40% with SASE. APAC reached 115%, up 800 basis points despite macros, via Singapore PDPA/cloud integrations and Japan ransomware rollback wins.

This validates our land-and-expand in a $200 billion market growing 15% CAGR in cloud security per IDC. $180 million in R&D this year, 22% of revenue, unlocks modules like GenAI Threat Hunting, tripling multi-module adoption to 75%. We see FY25 NDR at 120-125%, anchored by enterprise margins and regulated sectors.

On R&D investment, we allocated $265 million in Q3, or 21.2% of revenue—up 5 basis points sequentially and 150 from last year. Trailing twelve months: $568 million, 20.8% of $2.73 billion TTM revenue, exceeding FY23's 19.2% and rising from FY22's 18.1%. This matches or tops peers like CrowdStrike's 19-20% and Palo Alto's cloud push at 22%, fitting Gartner's $215 billion market outlook at 13.8% CAGR.

The increase stems from 22% R&D headcount growth to 1,800 engineers, including Check Point and Darktrace talent for AI/ML. Stock comp is 28% of spend, reported GAAP transparently.

Key projects: 35% to GuardAI Sentinel evolution—our next-gen XDR with generative AI for behavioral analytics and autonomous response against Log4Shell supply chains and LLM exploits, up 40% per MITRE, yielding 65% faster detection/response in pilots. 25% to SASE with post-quantum crypto like Kyber/Dilithium ahead of NIST 2024. 20% to Kubernetes security for EKS/AKS and EDR deception tech amid 300% cloud misconfigs per Unit 42. Remainder to homomorphic encryption for regulated data protection.

Distributed: 42% Israel for offensive sims/behavioral AI; 35% U.S. for Splunk/Elastic integrations; 15% EMEA for DORA/NIS2 against 93% ransomware rise per Sophos; 8% APAC for sovereign clouds and Australia's Essential Eight.

At 20-22%—above 17% industry per Bessemer—this builds moats with 3x SOC efficiency and 125% top-customer expansion. FY24 holds 20.5-22%, easing to 19-21% FY25 on pipeline scale, funded by $850 million cash, no debt.

Before Q&A, on FY25 guidance—revenue $4.85-$4.95 billion, 18-21% growth; ARR $4.6-$4.7 billion, 20-23%; non-GAAP op margins +250 bps to 32%; EPS $5.85-$6.05—these rest on macro, market, customer, and execution assumptions.

Macro: 2.5-3% global GDP, U.S. rates at 4% post-Fed cuts; cyber as must-have despite 8% IT spend per Gartner; 10-15% deal scrutiny but Q4 $180 million net new ARR proves ROI. Geopolitics: 25% nation-state attacks per Mandiant boost ShieldChain 40% ACV.

Market: $215-$275 billion TAM by 2028 at 13% CAGR; SAM 15%. Cloud/SASE 25% growth to $1.2 billion, gaining on Zscaler via EdgeFort. AI threats up 75% per CrowdStrike, 30% suite growth to $800 million with EU AI Act. Ransomware +20%, EDR/MDR 22%.

Customers: NDR 115-117%; enterprise 15% logos, ACV $450K +12%, 70% ZTA upsell; SMB 25% via Ingram; 20% expansions minus 5% pruning.

Regions: U.S. 55%/16%, CISA/CPRA; EMEA 25%/22%, NIS2; APAC 15%/28%, DPDP; ROW 5%/18%; 2% forex drag.

Execution: 18% R&D ($880 million) for PQC/CASB; $500 million M&A, AWS/MSFT 15% pipeline; margins 82% +100 bps, 65% CAC payback.

Risks: ±2% revenue; recession 10% H2 deals (75% book-to-bill mitigates); 5% ASP erosion offset bundling; semis 2%; regs. Upside: quantum/breaches +$200 million ARR.

Grounded in FY24 beats and $6.2 billion pipeline versus $4.88 million breach costs per IBM.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press * then 1 to queue a question. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex or Maria, can you expand on the NDR drivers, particularly expansions in APAC, and how that informs FY25 expectations?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Our 122% NDR reflects strong cohort retention and upsells, as Maria detailed. In APAC, despite headwinds, we hit 115% through PDPA-compliant clouds and ransomware features, with Japan banks adding rollback tech. This land-and-expand supports 120-125% FY25, focused on regulated verticals for resilience.

Operator: Next question from Emily Davis with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Davis: Great results. Maria, on guidance, what are the biggest assumptions around macro slowdowns and how sensitive is the midpoint?

Maria Chen: Emily, thanks. We've assumed moderate GDP and rate stabilization, with cyber decoupled from cycles—Q4 ARR proves it. Stress-tested for recession delaying 10% H2, but 75% book-to-bill cushions. Midpoint has ±2% tolerance; geo-tensions add tailwinds via supply chain urgency.

Operator: Next from Mike Lee with JPMorgan.

Mike Lee: Raj, on the Sentinel QuantumShield, how does it differentiate from peers on post-quantum threats, and any early traction?

Dr. Raj Patel: Mike, good question. QuantumShield embeds Kyber/Dilithium natively, processing petabytes for harvest-now risks ahead of NIST. Beta MTTD down 40%, false positives 0.3%—beats Cortex. Traction with financials/OEMs; FY25 50% XDR growth target.

Operator: Final question from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong: Strong R&D commitment. Maria or Alex, how does the 21% spend allocate across regions, and does it risk near-term margins?

Maria Chen: Lisa, our 21.2% is strategic—42% Israel AI, 35% U.S. integrations, etc., mirroring threats/talent. Funds Sentinel/SASE innovations for 3x efficiency, supporting margin expansion to 32%. Organic funding keeps FCF path to 25%+ intact.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
